cells.tense: The charge is happening now and you have the pen for it.
cells.act: follow a raw curiosity with no use for it
cells.ask: Take up whatever curiosity about this shared world is genuinely live in you and spend an afternoon on it with nothing to show for it after.
cells.core:
You move first in this shared world, and it fits. When something wants changing, you start it, and anyone standing nearby can feel where you stand. In the same stretch you're easy with not having the answer — you take things in before you decide what they are, and what you come away knowing tends to be right. That's the balance: the leading and the listening share the same ground.

The invitation in it is to feed the listening side on purpose. Take up whatever curiosity about this shared world is genuinely live in you and spend an afternoon on it with nothing to show for it after. Nothing needs to come of it. You'll find out what knowing looks like when it isn't asked to do anything, and the room will still be there when you come back.
cells.sheetLine: You start things, and you can be wrong where it counts.

cells.tense: The charge is aimed past the shared thing before it can take its shape.
cells.act: cut to the logic and act on it
cells.ask: Before the next move on this shared thing, cut to the logic in a single written line, then leave that line a day before you charge from it.
cells.core:
Where a shared meaning is being held between people, you're already several moves out. You've sorted where it should land and how fast, and the reasoned-out version of it precedes the messy one that actually forms when people hold it together. It's sharp and it's fast. The trouble is that a meaning needs the slow part, and cutting straight to the answer can settle for the room what it hasn't settled yet.

Before the next move on this shared thing, cut to the logic in a single written line, then leave that line a day before you charge from it. One line makes you put down the rest — the second and third and fourth setups. The pattern you're seeing is probably right. What a shared meaning offers back is that it gets built by more than one hand.

cells.tense: You had your hand on this shared thing once, and you left it at the door.
cells.act: move the structure one real inch
cells.ask: Move one real inch of the shared thing that's gone stale by steady, plain work, and keep the whole thing to yourself.
cells.core:
Where a shared meaning is held between people, your charge isn't in it. Somewhere earlier the move that was yours got set down, and now you stand at the edge of it — watching, not weighing in, letting the thing stay as it is. You may even be the one who cares most. From the outside it looks like keeping the peace; from where you stand, the ground feels like it belongs to somebody else.

Don't try to feel your way back. Move one real inch of the shared thing that's gone stale by steady, plain work, and keep the whole thing to yourself. Small, concrete, finished. Then let the next inch show itself before you go near the big question. This kind of change arrives by work, and it turns out you were not shut out of it.

cells.tense: You're setting the terms of the shared thing and calling it how things already are.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Separate the old way here into what's finished and what still serves, and put the finished part down with nothing owed to it.
cells.core:
You're doing the work already — deciding what goes and what stays in this shared world, taking the hit for the call, keeping what has outlived its moment. Ask and you'd say you only did what needed doing. That's the mechanism going without your name on it: the deciding is happening, the responsibility is running through you, and none of it is filed as yours.

Separate the old way here into what's finished and what still serves, and put the finished part down with nothing owed to it. Leave both halves where you can see them for a week without acting on either. Naming what you're already releasing is the whole act — it asks nothing of how you feel about it.
